name: Fruit and veg smell diet
lead: The fruit and veg smell diet is the practice of eating more fruit and vegetables in the belief that it makes sweat smell more pleasant. Wikipedia reports a study of males in which higher fruit and vegetable intake was associated with more pleasant-smelling sweat, described as floral, fruity, sweet and medicinal in quality.[1]
Grokipedia likewise says these foods have been associated with more pleasant body odors, but notes the scents are not typically strong.[2]
infobox: Zuniga et al., 2017 (diet quality and male body odor attractiveness)

paras: The Wikipedia body odor article lists Zuniga and colleagues (2017) on diet quality and the attractiveness of male body odor.[1] Sample details are not given in the pages consulted.[2]

Observational and sample-based research on male body odor and diet exists, as above; no interventional trial is described in the sources consulted. The association reported is not by itself evidence that dietary change causes the difference.[1][2]

timeline.event: Zuniga et al. publish on diet quality and attractiveness of male body odor.[1]

card.summary: Eating more fruit and vegetables is associated with more pleasant-smelling sweat in a study of men; effects are described as mild.
card.note: Association from a small body of work.

quick.overview:
Some people eat more fruit and vegetables hoping to smell better. A study of men found higher intake associated with sweat rated as more pleasant.

Sources describe the scents as mild.
quick.mechanism: Dietary compounds appear in sweat and may alter its perceived scent; the specific mechanism is not detailed in the sources consulted.
quick.risks: No risks documented in the sources consulted.
